decisions.reason: As a newly launched but less prominent consumer product with weaker fit to the firm's engineering-centered core, it is the most likely to fall below aspiration levels and be cut so resources can be redirected to core technology ventures.

This modular extension line fits the established business closely, benefits from the firm's technical and prototyping capabilities, and would likely be retained while management learns about demand across models.

Because it is both strongly aligned with the existing offer and explicitly presented as a flagship, management would tolerate early uncertainty and keep supporting it unless results clearly missed aspirations.

Although somewhat riskier than the core offer, its flagship status and strategic relevance to the firm's sustainable waste-conversion direction make retention more likely than withdrawal in the next year.
